name: Smart and bidirectional EV charging
summary: Charging software shifts electricity demand to better times, while compatible bidirectional systems can send energy from vehicle batteries to a building or the grid.
useCase: An electric delivery fleet charges overnight when power is cheaper and exports a contracted amount during an evening grid peak, retaining enough range for the next shift.
whyNow: The addressable equipment base is expanding rapidly: IEA reports that China’s public charging points increased from nearly 3.4 million at the end of 2024 to more than 4.7 million at the end of 2025. Public charging is an adjacent-market proxy here, because there is no consistent global census of active vehicle-to-grid installations. Managed charging can produce value without exporting power; bidirectional operation additionally needs a compatible vehicle, charger, building connection and market arrangement. The Mobility House’s 2026 decision to focus more closely on energy services illustrates the commercial importance of orchestration. Hardware capability alone does not establish paying participation or useful grid capacity.

mainstream.scope: Routine managed charging and commercially repeatable bidirectional offers for compatible vehicle fleets and households in electricity markets that compensate flexibility.
mainstream.rationale: Smart charging is already routine in some products. The later date applies to widespread, supportable bidirectional packages with clear warranties, interoperable equipment and predictable tariffs. Fleets with regular parking schedules are likely to scale earlier than every household. Tariff design and vehicle replacement cycles can keep many markets below this threshold in 2035.

metric.name: Public EV charging points in China: addressable-base proxy
metric.scope: China public light-duty charging network; includes ordinary charging and is not a V2G installation count.
metric.limitations: The proxy measures the broader charging ecosystem. Public sites often differ from the home/workplace locations best suited to bidirectional service. Do not read the historical or future line as smart-charging penetration.
metric.futureNote: IEA projects nearly 18 million Chinese public charging points in 2035 under both its Current Policies and Stated Policies scenarios. This is a charging-infrastructure scenario, not a bidirectional adoption forecast.

milestones.text: Vehicle-to-grid demonstrations predate the window; no harmonised global annual installed-base measure was retained.
Charging expansion and demonstration projects do not provide a comparable measure of active bidirectional customers; no annual value is interpolated.
No consistent global V2G deployment observation was found in the selected evidence; maturity is an analyst assessment, not a measured percentage.
China had nearly 3.4 million public charging points by year-end; these are all public points, not bidirectional installations.
China’s public stock exceeded 4.7 million points; global public stock exceeded 7 million. The charger base is growing faster than proven V2G participation.
The Mobility House announced sale of its Solutions unit to Edenred while focusing on its energy business; commercial charging and energy-service activities must be distinguished.

tailwinds: EV batteries form a growing pool of devices that may provide flexible demand or export.
Time-varying prices can reward charging shifts even without bidirectional hardware.
Predictable fleet schedules simplify availability commitments and optimisation.
bottlenecks: Vehicle, charger and utility interfaces must work together in real installations.
Battery warranties, customer mobility needs and reserve preferences constrain dispatch.
Installation, metering and connection costs may overwhelm household earnings.
watchMetrics: Enrolled compatible vehicles that actually delivered grid service, not vehicles advertised as capable.
Net customer savings after charger, installation and battery-related costs.
Delivered MW, availability, export duration and driver opt-outs during contracted events.
